key_insight: The paper shows that an AI system can act like a real scientific operator, autonomously aligning single crystals at a synchrotron X-ray beamline. In simple terms, large language models can help drive adaptive, closed-loop experiments in a live laboratory setting.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of manually aligning crystals and steering experiments at large-scale X-ray facilities, which is time-consuming, expert-dependent, and difficult to automate robustly.
method: Used an agentic AI system built around large language models to plan and execute beamline actions.
Connected the AI to a real synchrotron environment for closed-loop control and real-time decision-making.
Demonstrated autonomous single-crystal alignment as a proof of concept for adaptive scientific experimentation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this is a strong example of LLMs moving beyond text tasks into embodied scientific workflows. It highlights how agentic systems can support automation, reduce expert bottlenecks, and enable faster iterative discovery in complex physical environments.
visual_elements: A closed-loop workflow diagram showing sensing, reasoning, action, and feedback at the beamline.

paper_title: An agentic artificially intelligent X-ray scientist
paper_authors: Zhantao Chen, Alexander N. Petsch, Aidan J. Israelski, Rajan Plumley, Lingjia Shen
